articles.title: Guinea-Bissau approves new constitution as opposition calls referendum a fraud
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Guinea-Bissau has approved a new constitution that expands presidential powers, but the result has triggered a political dispute after opposition parties and groups rejected the referendum as illegitimate and accused the National Electoral Commission (CNE) of fabricating turnout figures. The constitutional referendum was held on August 30, less than a year after the military seized power following disputed presidential and legislative elections. According to provisional results announced by the CNE on September 1 , 70% of valid votes supported the new constitution, while 30% opposed it. Turnout was about 60%. articles.title: China is NOT abandoning Iran – Tehran journalist explains
articles.author: Amanda Yee
articles.content_excerpt: Since the beginning of the US-Israeli war on Iran, some have claimed that Beijing’s support for Tehran is little more than empty rhetoric and symbolic statements. So what is the nature of the China-Iran alliance? Tehran-based journalist Navid Zarrinnal joins Amanda Yee to give a realistic breakdown of China-Iran relations, the significance of the Bishkek Declaration coming out of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit, and why Beijing’s dismissal of Trump’s “economic D-day” sanctions represents a major defiance of the Washington-led order.
